small_guidance:
- Add more autotune configs targeting M=N=K=8192 fp32: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=16 and BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32 with num_stages=4-5; large K=8192 benefits from deeper pipelining to overlap loads.
- The softmax kernel with BLOCK_N=8192 fp32 forces 32KB/row in registers; try num_warps=16 or split into a two-pass (online) softmax with smaller BLOCK_N (e.g., 1024) to reduce register pressure and improve occupancy.
- Drop the per-K-iter `k_remaining` masking (M,N,K are all multiples of 128 here) by adding a `EVEN_K: tl.constexpr` branch in autotune to skip mask computation in the inner loop.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax max-reduction directly into the GEMM epilogue using a split-K-free, N-persistent strategy: have one program own a full row tile (BLOCK_M rows × full N) so it can compute GELU and the row max/sum in registers/SMEM without writing the intermediate `out_gelu` to HBM. This eliminates one full 1024×8192 fp32 write+read (~32MB round trip).
- Alternatively, make the softmax an online (single-pass) streaming kernel that reads `out_gelu` in tiles of BLOCK_N (e.g., 1024) updating running max and sum, then a second pass normalizes — avoids the giant 8192-wide register tile and lets num_warps stay at 8.
- Consider casting weights to tf32/bf16 for `tl.dot` (input fp32 with tf32 allowed) — on RTX 4090 (Ada) tf32 mma roughly doubles GEMM throughput vs. fp32 accumulation-from-fp32 paths; ensure `allow_tf32=True` and use `tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=True)`.
